request.description: 28-year-old renter in NYC earning $85k — high rent, no savings, no retirement contributions

recommendations.message: Your rent ($2,800) is 39.5% of your gross income — well above the recommended 30%. Consider finding a lower-cost apartment or a roommate.
You're not contributing to your 401(k). At minimum, contribute 3% to capture your full employer match — that's $212/month in free compensation you're leaving behind.
Your emergency fund target covers only 1 month of expenses. Aim for 3–6 months ($9,000–$18,000) to protect against job loss or unexpected costs.
Your non-mortgage debt payments ($400/month) are a significant burden. Consider accelerating payoff using the avalanche method (highest interest first).
You're spending $300/month dining out. Even reducing this by $100/month frees up $1,200/year for emergency savings or retirement.
